correctness.rationale: At each base coordinate z the two rows are independently in the span of (z²,z,1) and (2z,1,0). On the rank-two locus the derivative coefficients recover the ruling point, so this row-space model computes the degree of the actual tangent-plane incidence map. Its normal is [1:−2z:z²]. Away from characteristic two the annihilator discriminant gives H, recovering z rationally on M_0≠0. The rank-one locus cannot supply a hypersurface component and the displayed rank-two point has derivative ∂H/∂A_0=4, so H is geometrically prime in these characteristics. Along the rank-one divisor H lies in the square of its defining ideal; nonregularity in codimension one follows even over imperfect fields. In characteristic two the normals fill a dense part of the line M_1=0 geometrically, and Q is an irreducible 2-by-2 determinant. Its gradient ideal is exactly (A_0,A_2,B_0,B_2); codimension three of the singular locus and the hypersurface S_2 property give normality. On A_2=1, Q solves for B_0, and A_0 has valuation one at (A_0) in the resulting rational function field. Adjoining its square root gives the whole generic incidence field and purely inseparable degree two. Primitivity gives a torsion-free integral homogeneous-coordinate quotient and flatness, with special equation Q². This is a geometric image, not the closure of just the k-rational tangent planes. The supplied verifier and recorded output were inspected, not run; their finite samples are not needed for these arguments.

value.rationale: The balanced quartic scroll is a basic, fixed embedded test case for tangent schemes in mixed characteristic. The exact comparison separates three phenomena that an equation over characteristic zero alone misses: noncommutation with reduced image, the change in normality, and inseparable generic incidence despite a single geometric generic preimage. These are useful model-specific boundary data, not merely a modular polynomial expansion.
